subject: maths
title: Year 6 Converting Metric Units: Length, Mass and Capacity
seo_title: Year 6 Converting Metric Units Worksheets: mm, cm, m, km, g, kg, t, mL and L (Free Maths with Answer Key)
standard_text: Convert between common metric units of length, mass and capacity; choose and use decimal representations of metric measurements relevant to the situation
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on converting metric units, aligned to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M6M01): mm, cm, m and km, g, kg and t, mL and L with decimals, choosing sensible units, comparing mixed units and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Bigger unit to smaller unit: multiply. Smaller unit to bigger unit: divide.
body_html:
Multiply or divide?

To change a bigger unit into a smaller unit, multiply: you need more of the small units. To change a smaller unit into a bigger unit, divide. Multiplying by 1000 moves every digit 3 places to the left. Dividing by 1000 moves every digit 3 places to the right.

Metres to centimetres

1.25 m = ☐ cm

1 m = 100 cm. Multiply: 1.25 × 100 = 125.

Answer: 125 cm

Grams to kilograms

750 g = ☐ kg

1 kg = 1000 g. Divide: 750 ÷ 1000 = 0.75.

Answer: 0.75 kg

Litres to millilitres

2.5 L = ☐ mL

1 L = 1000 mL. Multiply: 2.5 × 1000 = 2500.

Answer: 2500 mL

Facts to know

MeasureFacts
Length1 cm = 10 mm   1 m = 100 cm = 1000 mm   1 km = 1000 m
Mass1 kg = 1000 g   1 t = 1000 kg
Capacity1 L = 1000 mL

Choose a sensible unit and decimal form

Pick the unit that gives an easy number for the situation. A board is 2.45 m, not 0.002 45 km. An ant is 6 mm, not 0.006 m. Two units together can be written as one decimal.

Two units as a decimal

3 kg 40 g = ☐ kg

40 g = 40 ÷ 1000 = 0.04 kg. Keep the 0 in the tenths place.

Answer: 3.04 kg (not 3.4 kg)

Read the scale, then convert

Compare in one unit

To compare or order, change every measurement into the same unit first.

Which is longer?

0.5 km or 5200 cm?

0.5 km = 500 m. 5200 cm = 52 m. 500 m is longer.

Answer: 0.5 km

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
2.5 kg = 250 g (multiplying by 100)1 kg = 1000 g, so 2.5 kg = 2500 g
750 g = 750 000 kg (moving the point the wrong way)Smaller unit to bigger unit: divide. 750 g = 0.75 kg
1.5 m = 105 cm1.5 m is 1 m 50 cm, so 1.5 m = 150 cm
3 kg 40 g = 3.4 kg40 g = 0.04 kg, so 3 kg 40 g = 3.04 kg
Comparing only the numbers (5200 cm > 0.5 km)Use one unit first: 5200 cm = 52 m and 0.5 km = 500 m

faq.q: What metric conversions do Year 6 students learn in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 6 students convert between mm, cm, m and km, between g, kg and t, and between mL and L, and they use decimals such as 1.25 m = 125 cm and 750 g = 0.75 kg.

faq.q: How do you convert 1.5 m to centimetres?
faq.a: Multiply by 100, because 1 m = 100 cm: 1.5 × 100 = 150 cm. It is not 105 cm, because 0.5 m is half a metre, 50 cm.

faq.q: How many kilograms are in a tonne?
faq.a: 1 tonne = 1000 kg. So a 2.4 t truck load is 2.4 × 1000 = 2400 kg, and 3500 kg = 3.5 t.

faq.q: Is converting metric units tested in NAPLAN?
faq.a: Year 6 students do not sit NAPLAN, but measurement, including converting units, is part of the NAPLAN numeracy test in Years 7 and 9. Practising it in Year 6 is good preparation for high school.

sets.title: Length: mm, cm, m and km with decimals

items.q: Convert. 3.6 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 3.6 × 100 = 360. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 3.6 m = 360 cm.

items.q: Convert. 1.25 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1.25 × 100 = 125. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 1.25 m = 125 cm.

items.q: Convert. 1.5 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1.5 × 100 = 150. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 1.5 m = 150 cm. (1.5 m is 1 m 50 cm, so it is not 105 cm. 105 cm would be 1.05 m.)

items.q: Convert. 45 mm = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Millimetres are smaller than centimetres, so divide by 10: 45 ÷ 10 = 4.5. The digits move 1 place to the right. So 45 mm = 4.5 cm.

items.q: Convert. 2.4 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1000: 2.4 × 1000 = 2400. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.4 km = 2400 m.

items.q: Convert. 850 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1000: 850 ÷ 1000 = 0.85. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 850 m = 0.85 km. (850 000 km multiplies when it should divide.)

items.q: Convert. 0.7 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 0.7 × 10 = 7. The digits move 1 place to the left. So 0.7 cm = 7 mm.

items.q: Convert. 65 cm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Centimetres are smaller than metres, so divide by 100: 65 ÷ 100 = 0.65. The digits move 2 places to the right. So 65 cm = 0.65 m.

items.q: Convert. 3.125 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1000: 3.125 × 1000 = 3125. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3.125 km = 3125 m.

items.q: Convert. 75 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1000: 75 ÷ 1000 = 0.075. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 75 m = 0.075 km. Check: 0.75 km would be 750 m.

items.q: Convert. 1.75 m = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 m = 1000 mm. Metres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 1000: 1.75 × 1000 = 1750. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1.75 m = 1750 mm. (1.75 × 100 = 175 would give centimetres, not millimetres.)

items.q: Convert. 45 mm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 1000 mm. Millimetres are smaller than metres, so divide by 1000: 45 ÷ 1000 = 0.045. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 45 mm = 0.045 m. You need a 0 in the tenths place.
The pencil ends 3 small marks after 8 cm. Each small mark is 1 mm, so it is 83 mm. 1 cm = 10 mm, so 83 ÷ 10 = 8.3 cm.
The crayon ends 6 small marks after 5 cm, so it is 56 mm. 1 m = 1000 mm, so divide by 1000: 56 ÷ 1000 = 0.056 m. (0.56 m divides by 100, which gives 560 mm.)

items.q: Convert. 4050 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1000: 4050 ÷ 1000 = 4.05. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 4050 m = 4.05 km. The 0 in 4050 keeps its place: 4.05, not 4.5.

items.q: Convert. 1.08 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1.08 × 100 = 108. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 1.08 m = 108 cm.

items.q: Convert. 2 km 75 m = ☐ km
Which is the same as 0.305 km?
items.e: Multiply by 1000: 0.305 × 1000 = 305 m. The 0 holds the tenths place, so it is not 35 m.

items.q: Which is the same as 6.04 m?
Find the missing number. 1 km − 375 m = ☐ km

sets.title: Mass and capacity: g, kg, t, mL and L

items.q: Convert. 750 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1000: 750 ÷ 1000 = 0.75. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 750 g = 0.75 kg.

items.q: Convert. 2.5 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1000: 2.5 × 1000 = 2500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.5 kg = 2500 g. (250 g multiplies by 100, but 1 kg is 1000 g, not 100 g.)

items.q: Convert. 1.25 L = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 1.25 × 1000 = 1250. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1.25 L = 1250 mL. (125 mL would be 0.125 L.)

items.q: Convert. 2.5 L = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 2.5 × 1000 = 2500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.5 L = 2500 mL.

items.q: Convert. 330 mL = ☐ L
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1000: 330 ÷ 1000 = 0.33. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 330 mL = 0.33 L.

items.q: Convert. 2.4 t = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 t = 1000 kg. Tonnes are bigger than kilograms, so multiply by 1000: 2.4 × 1000 = 2400. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.4 t = 2400 kg. (240 kg multiplies by 100, but 1 t is 1000 kg.)

items.q: Convert. 3500 kg = ☐ t
items.e: 1 t = 1000 kg. Kilograms are smaller than tonnes, so divide by 1000: 3500 ÷ 1000 = 3.5. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 3500 kg = 3.5 t.

items.q: Convert. 45 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1000: 45 ÷ 1000 = 0.045. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 45 g = 0.045 kg.

items.q: Convert. 4.08 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1000: 4.08 × 1000 = 4080. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 4.08 kg = 4080 g.

items.q: Convert. 0.6 t = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 t = 1000 kg. Tonnes are bigger than kilograms, so multiply by 1000: 0.6 × 1000 = 600. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.6 t = 600 kg.

items.q: Convert. 2600 mL = ☐ L
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1000: 2600 ÷ 1000 = 2.6. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 2600 mL = 2.6 L.

items.q: Convert. 0.08 L = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 0.08 × 1000 = 80. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.08 L = 80 mL.

items.q: Convert. 3 kg 50 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 50 g = 50 ÷ 1000 = 0.05 kg. So 3 kg 50 g = 3.05 kg. 3.5 kg would be 3 kg 500 g.

items.q: Work out 1.5 kg + 700 g. Give your answer in kilograms.
items.e: Use one unit first: 700 g = 0.7 kg. Then 1.5 + 0.7 = 2.2 kg. 701.5 kg adds the numbers without converting.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of flour. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 5 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 5 = 0.2 kg (200 g). The needle is 2 marks past 1 kg: 1 + 0.4 = 1.4 kg. (1.2 kg counts each mark as 0.1 kg.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a parcel. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 4 = 0.25 kg (250 g). The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 2 + 0.75 = 2.75 kg. (2.3 kg counts each mark as 0.1 kg.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of some apples. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: The needle points to 600 g. 1 kg = 1000 g, so divide by 1000: 600 ÷ 1000 = 0.6 kg.

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in litres.
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mL with 5 spaces between them, so each line is 100 mL. The water is 3 lines above 1000 mL: 1300 mL. 1300 ÷ 1000 = 1.3 L. (1.03 L would be 1030 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in litres.
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL with 5 spaces between them, so each line is 50 mL. The water is 3 lines above 500 mL: 500 + 150 = 650 mL. 650 ÷ 1000 = 0.65 L. (0.53 L counts each line as 10 mL.)

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 2 L?
items.e: Each line is 100 mL. The water is at 1600 mL. 2 L = 2000 mL. 2000 − 1600 = 400 mL more. (600 mL reads the water level as 1400 mL.)

sets.title: Choose a sensible unit and decimal form

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the mass of a watermelon?
items.e: A watermelon is heavy to carry but far lighter than a car, so kilograms fit. 4.5 g is lighter than one 20c coin, and 4.5 t is heavier than a big car.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for how much a can of soft drink holds?
items.e: A can holds less than half a litre. 375 mL = 0.375 L. 375 L would fill a big bathtub twice.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the length of a classroom?
items.e: A classroom is about 10 big steps long, so 9.5 m fits. 9.5 cm is only the width of a hand, and 95 m is longer than a whole row of classrooms.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the mass of a loaded truck?
items.e: A loaded truck is very heavy, so use tonnes. 12.5 t = 12 500 kg.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the driving distance from Sydney to Canberra?
items.e: Sydney to Canberra is a drive of about 3 hours, so it is a few hundred kilometres. 2.9 km is only a short walk.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the thickness of a mobile phone?
items.e: A phone is thinner than 1 cm, so use millimetres. 8 cm is as thick as a large book.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for how much water a bathtub holds?
items.e: A bathtub holds a lot of water, so use litres. 1.5 L is only a large drink bottle.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the mass of an adult koala?
items.e: An adult koala is about as heavy as a big bag of dog food, so kilograms fit. 0.9 kg = 900 g, which is lighter than a carton of milk.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the mass of a Year 6 student?
items.e: Most Year 6 students have a mass of about 30 kg to 50 kg. 3.8 kg is the mass of a new baby.

items.q: A carpenter measures a board as 2 m 45 cm. How is this written in metres?
A bag of rice has a mass of 1650 g. Which shows this in kilograms?
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g, so divide by 1000: 1650 ÷ 1000 = 1.65 kg. (16.5 kg divides by 100, as if 1 kg were 100 g.)

items.q: A jug holds 1 L 200 mL. Which shows this in litres?
Which shows 3 kg 250 g using one unit?
items.e: 250 g = 0.25 kg, so 3 kg 250 g = 3.25 kg (or 3250 g). 325 g joins the digits and loses the 0.

items.q: A newborn baby has a mass of 3 kg 40 g. Which shows this in kilograms?
items.e: 40 g = 40 ÷ 1000 = 0.04 kg. So 3 kg 40 g = 3.04 kg. 3.4 kg would be 3 kg 400 g.

items.q: A bridge sign shows a mass limit of 4500 kg. Which shows this in tonnes?
items.e: 1 t = 1000 kg, so divide by 1000: 4500 ÷ 1000 = 4.5 t. (45 t divides by 100.)

items.q: Mia jumps 312 cm in the long jump. Which shows this in metres?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so divide by 100: 312 ÷ 100 = 3.12 m. The digits move 2 places to the right.

items.q: An ant is 0.006 m long. Which shows the same length in a more sensible unit?
items.e: 1 m = 1000 mm, so 0.006 × 1000 = 6 mm. A small number of millimetres is easier to read than a decimal with zeros.

items.q: A road is 0.004 km wide. Which shows the same width in a more sensible unit?
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m, so 0.004 × 1000 = 4 m. Metres suit the width of a road.

items.q: Which decimal measurement is the same as 2 L 50 mL?
A cricket oval is 1 km 60 m around the outside. Which shows this in kilometres?
items.e: 60 m = 60 ÷ 1000 = 0.06 km. So 1 km 60 m = 1.06 km. 1.6 km would be 1 km 600 m.

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to metres: 0.5 km = 500 m, 5200 cm = 52 m and 0.48 km = 480 m. 500 m is the longest. 5200 cm has the biggest number, but centimetres are small.

items.q: Which is the shortest?
items.e: Change them all to millimetres: 6.5 cm = 65 mm, 0.07 m = 70 mm and 0.6 m = 600 mm. 65 mm is the shortest.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1.2 kg = 1200 g, 0.95 kg = 950 g and 1 kg 150 g = 1150 g. 1200 g is the heaviest.

items.q: Which is the lightest?
items.e: Change them all to kilograms: 0.3 t = 300 kg and 0.32 t = 320 kg. 300 kg is the lightest. 3100 kg is 3.1 t, the heaviest of all.

items.q: Which holds the most?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 1.5 L = 1500 mL, 0.9 L = 900 mL and 1 L 450 mL = 1450 mL. 1500 mL is the most.

items.q: Which holds the least?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 0.75 L = 750 mL and 0.8 L = 800 mL. 700 mL is the least.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to kilograms: 0.07 t = 0.07 × 1000 = 70 kg and 7500 g = 7.5 kg. 70 kg is the heaviest. 7500 g has the biggest number, but grams are small.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1.2 × 1000 = 1200, so 1.2 km = 1200 m. The others are wrong: 0.3 m = 30 cm, 45 mm = 0.045 m and 2.5 m = 2500 mm.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 0.6 × 1000 = 600, so 0.6 kg = 600 g. The others are wrong: 1.05 L = 1050 mL, and 3 t = 3000 kg, which is less than 3100 kg.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 0.75 kg = 750 g, and 750 g > 705 g. The others are wrong: 0.5 L = 500 mL, 2.4 t = 2400 kg and 1.5 m = 150 cm.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 3.5 km = 3500 m, and 3500 m > 3050 m. The others are wrong: 0.8 m = 80 cm, 0.3 kg = 300 g and 1.25 L = 1250 mL.

items.q: Which list goes from the smallest to the largest capacity?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 0.25 L = 250 mL and 0.5 L = 500 mL. 250 < 400 < 500.

items.q: Which list goes from the shortest to the longest?
items.e: Change them all to metres: 0.09 km = 90 m and 9600 cm = 96 m. 90 < 95 < 96.

items.q: Which list goes from the heaviest to the lightest?
items.e: Change them all to kilograms: 2.5 t = 2500 kg and 2.25 t = 2250 kg. 2500 > 2250 > 2050. 2.25 is not more than 2.5: compare the tenths first.

items.q: Put these in order from shortest to longest: 1.2 m, 125 cm, 1150 mm, 0.13 km
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 1.2 m = 120 cm, 1150 mm = 115 cm and 0.13 km = 130 m = 13 000 cm. 115 < 120 < 125 < 13 000. (0.13 km has the smallest number but is by far the longest.)

items.q: Which is not the same as 1.2 km?
Which two measurements are equal?
How much longer is 1.5 m than 105 cm?
items.e: Use one unit: 1.5 m = 150 cm. 150 − 105 = 45 cm. (1395 cm treats 1.5 m as 1500 cm, and 0.45 cm puts the wrong unit on 0.45 m.)

items.q: How much more is 2 L than 1250 mL?
items.e: Use one unit: 2 L = 2000 mL. 2000 − 1250 = 750 mL. (1248 mL takes away 2 without converting, and 3250 mL adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: Lachlan says 0.5 kg is less than 450 g, because 0.5 is smaller than 450. Is he right?
c: Yes. 0.5 kg = 5 g, which is less.
No. 0.5 kg = 50 g, so they are equal.
No. 0.5 kg = 500 g, which is more than 450 g.
items.e: Compare in the same unit. 0.5 × 1000 = 500, so 0.5 kg = 500 g, and 500 g > 450 g.

sets.title: Word problems: recipes, fun runs, water bottles and trucks

items.q: The school fun run is 5 km. It goes around a 400 m track. How many laps is that?
items.e: 5 km = 5000 m. 5000 ÷ 400 = 12.5 laps. Check: 12 × 400 = 4800 m, and half a lap is 200 m more.

items.q: Charlotte has run 3.2 km of the 5 km fun run. How many metres does she have left?
Oliver makes pancakes. One batch needs 0.3 kg of flour. He makes 3 batches from a 1.5 kg bag. How many grams of flour are left?
items.e: 3 × 0.3 = 0.9 kg used. 1.5 − 0.9 = 0.6 kg left. 0.6 × 1000 = 600 g. (1200 g only takes away one batch.)

items.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 250 mL of milk. How many litres of milk are needed for 10 people?
items.e: 250 ÷ 4 = 62.5 mL for each person. 10 × 62.5 = 625 mL. 625 ÷ 1000 = 0.625 L. (2.5 L uses 250 mL for each person.)

items.q: An Anzac biscuit recipe uses 125 g of butter to make 12 biscuits. Isla wants to make 36 biscuits. How many kilograms of butter does she need?
items.e: 36 biscuits is 3 times 12, so 3 × 125 = 375 g. 375 ÷ 1000 = 0.375 kg. (3.75 kg divides by 100.)

items.q: Noah drinks 4 full 750 mL water bottles on a hot day. How many litres is that?
How many 600 mL bottles can be filled from a 15 L water cooler?
items.e: 15 L = 15 000 mL. 15 000 ÷ 600 = 25 bottles. Check: 25 × 600 = 15 000 mL. (40 bottles divides 600 by 15.)

items.q: 25 students each take a 750 mL water bottle on an excursion. How many litres of water is that altogether?
items.e: 25 × 750 = 18 750 mL. 18 750 ÷ 1000 = 18.75 L. (187.5 L divides by 100, and 18 750 L forgets to change millilitres into litres.)

items.q: A small truck can carry 2.4 t. Each bag of cement has a mass of 40 kg. How many bags can it carry?
items.e: 2.4 t = 2400 kg. 2400 ÷ 40 = 60 bags. (6 bags uses 2.4 t = 240 kg, and 96 bags multiplies 2.4 × 40.)

items.q: An empty truck has a mass of 2.4 t. It is loaded with 850 kg of bricks. What is the total mass in tonnes?
items.e: 850 kg = 850 ÷ 1000 = 0.85 t. 2.4 + 0.85 = 3.25 t. (10.9 t treats 850 kg as 8.5 t, and 852.4 t adds without converting.)

items.q: A truck carries 2.4 t of sand. It drops off 650 kg at each of 3 houses. How much sand is left, in kilograms?
items.e: 2.4 t = 2400 kg. 3 × 650 = 1950 kg dropped off. 2400 − 1950 = 450 kg left. (1750 kg takes away only one load, and 1950 kg is the sand dropped off.)

items.q: Jack posts three parcels: 1.25 kg, 750 g and 2.4 kg. What is their total mass in kilograms?
items.e: Change 750 g to kilograms first: 750 ÷ 1000 = 0.75 kg. 1.25 + 0.75 + 2.4 = 4.4 kg. (11.15 kg treats 750 g as 7.5 kg.)

items.q: At the athletics carnival, Oliver jumps 1.6 m, Ava jumps 155 cm, Leo jumps 1580 mm and Ruby jumps 1.06 m. Who jumps the furthest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 1.6 m = 160 cm, 1580 mm = 158 cm and 1.06 m = 106 cm. 160 cm is the furthest, so Oliver jumps the furthest.

items.q: Kai swims 1.2 km at training in a 25 m pool. How many lengths does he swim?
items.e: 1.2 km = 1200 m. 1200 ÷ 25 = 48 lengths. Check: 48 × 25 = 1200. (24 lengths counts there and back, 50 m, as one length.)

items.q: Grace has 4.5 m of ribbon. She cuts it into pieces 15 cm long. How many pieces does she get?
items.e: 4.5 m = 450 cm. 450 ÷ 15 = 30 pieces. (3 pieces divides 45 by 15 without converting.)

items.q: A school bushwalk is 12 km. The class walks 2.75 km before lunch and 3600 m after lunch. How much further do they still have to walk?
A 2 L carton of juice is poured into 8 cups of 180 mL each. How many millilitres are left in the carton?
items.e: 8 × 180 = 1440 mL poured. 2 L = 2000 mL. 2000 − 1440 = 560 mL left. (1820 mL takes away only one cup.)

items.q: A box of 24 apples has a mass of 3.6 kg. Each apple has the same mass. What is the mass of one apple in grams?
items.e: 3.6 kg = 3600 g. 3600 ÷ 24 = 150 g. (15 g changes 3.6 kg into 360 g, and 86.4 g multiplies 3.6 × 24.)

items.q: The canteen buys 6 kg of sausages for a sausage sizzle. Each sausage has a mass of 75 g. How many sausages is that?
items.e: 6 kg = 6000 g. 6000 ÷ 75 = 80 sausages. Check: 80 × 75 = 6000. (450 sausages multiplies 6 × 75.)

items.q: Ava was 1.38 m tall last year. Since then she has grown 6 cm. How tall is she now, in metres?
